title: AI tells -- formatting and punctuation
description: Markup and punctuation tells. These decay slowly, but em-dash suppression shipped in late-2025 frontier models, so ABSENCE proves nothing while density still signals.

rules.name: Keep only the em dashes that mark a real aside
rules.message: dash density: {match} dashes per 1000 words -- most become commas, colons, or two sentences
rules.fix: Convert each dash that is not marking a real aside into a comma, a colon, or two sentences.

citation.note: The catalog's tell is DENSITY, not presence, and this is the metric form of it. Deliberately counts the ASCII `--` form as well as U+2014/U+2013, which is what makes it usable in a repo whose house style writes `--`: the catalog's "Hyphen-swap" row says a find-and-replace on a tell is still the tell, and the measured `--`-to-dash ratio in the source corpus is 6,743 to 2,124. Threshold 6 per 1000 words is INFERRED from the catalog's "several dramatic pivots per page" and is NOT measured -- calibrate before enforcing outside strict. prose-format.no-unicode-dash bans the Unicode characters outright and is the presence rule; this is the density rule, and they are complements. https://github.com/srobroek/slopvac/blob/18c37dcaf2d11ef43ab9cf4610cae0664e2644af/packages/slopvac-lint/docs/exclusions.md records why upstream ai-tells.EmDashUsage is disabled.

rules.name: Use sentence case in headings
rules.message: title-case heading: {match} -- use sentence case unless house style says otherwise
rules.fix: Lower-case every word but the first and any proper noun.

citation.source: AI tells catalog — formatting.md ("Title Case In Every Heading")
citation.note:
The catalog itself concedes the house-style escape ("unless house style says otherwise"), so this is advisory everywhere and excluded at relaxed. The pattern accepts a heading of two or more capitalised words, letting a closed list of function words, all-caps initialisms, code spans, digits, and punctuation through; it cannot distinguish a title-cased heading from one that is mostly proper nouns ("Oh My Pi", "Claude Code"), which is why it never reaches enforced. Recalibrated in the 2026-09-12 audit: the earlier three-plain-words form matched 5 of 143 AI headings and 0 of 191 human; this one matches 30 of 143 AI and 16 of 191 human, the human hits being proper nouns.
Only plain capitalised words after the first count (`Server`, not `SDK`, `EventLog`, `gRPC`, `Python3` or a code span), so a heading whose only capitals are acronyms or identifiers passes (issue #257). `ALLOWED_WORDS` in the pattern is a placeholder that matches nothing real; rules.inject_locale_rule swaps in the `[locale] allow` words so a project can declare its proper nouns.

rules.name: Bold at most the first definitional use
rules.message: bold spray: {match} bold spans per 1000 words -- bold at most first definitional use
rules.fix: Keep bold on the first definitional use of a term and delete the rest.

citation.note: Density metric, matching the catalog's shape ("every occurrence of chosen terms bolded"). Threshold 20 per 1000 words was set in the 2026-09-12 audit: measured bold density was 2.64 per 1000 words on pre-2022 human prose, 6.32 on unguided model prose; the earlier threshold of 10 fired on 2 of 11 human documents, 20 on none while still catching 2 of 17 model documents. The catalog's "key takeaway" styling half is heading content, not bold density.

rules.name: Convert a repeated bold-colon bullet run to prose or a table
rules.message: inline-header list: {match} consecutive bold-colon bullets -- prose, or a table with real columns
rules.fix: Rewrite as prose, or as a table when there are real columns.

citation.note: This is the mechanizable SHAPE half of two catalog entries: formatting.md's "Inline-header list" and structure.md's "Bold-lead-in bullet symmetry". The content half -- whether the bullets carry distinct substance -- is ai-tells-structure.tricolon-abuse-remainder, and the document-level framing judgement is ai-tells-register.over-formatting-reflex. Threshold 4 is INFERRED from the structure catalog's "x 6" illustration; calibrate.

rules.name: Fix a skipped heading level
rules.message: heading hierarchy: {match} -- fix the level; delete the rule before it
rules.fix: Use the next level down, and delete any horizontal rule immediately before a heading.

citation.source: AI tells catalog — formatting.md ("Skipped heading levels; horizontal rules before headings")
citation.note: kind=structure, because the check is block-level shape over the heading sequence, not a regex over text: it needs the previous heading's level. Two defects in one rule, matching the catalog row -- an H2 followed by an H4, and a horizontal rule immediately preceding a heading. Enforced at every tier: a skipped level breaks screen-reader navigation and every TOC generator, which makes it an accessibility defect rather than a register preference. No existing Vale rule covers it, ours or upstream.

rules.name: Unwrap a table that holds one sentence

match.question: Does each table in this document have at least two rows whose cells vary in the same dimension, or is it one sentence in a grid?

examples.bad:
| Note |
|---|
| The loader reads the lockfile. |

rules.fix: Unwrap the table into the sentence it holds.

citation.source: AI tells catalog — formatting.md ("Tables wrapping what is actually one sentence of prose")
citation.note: Judgement, because a one-row table is legitimate as a header-only reference stub and the test is whether the cells vary in a shared dimension. Inverse of prose-format.prose-block, which flags prose that should have been a table.

rules.name: Delete manufactured emphasis
rules.message: italicised copula: {match} -- delete the emphasis; let word order carry the contrast

examples.good: The loader caches every resolved path.

rules.fix: Delete the emphasis; rewrite so word order carries the contrast if it is real.

citation.source: AI tells catalog — formatting.md ("Italicised copula for manufactured profundity")
citation.note: Fully mechanizable: the tell is a closed set of function words under emphasis. `scope: raw` because the marker characters are markdown syntax that the prose parser strips. Upstream ai-tells.EmphaticCopula covers this and stays enabled, so expect duplicates. GO->PYTHON REGEX NOTE: uses two lookbehinds, unsupported by Go RE2; the upstream rule must reach the same lines another way.

rules.name: Delete the cross-reference signpost
rules.message: cross-reference signposting: {match} -- delete it; a doc with a TOC is not read linearly

examples.bad: As mentioned above, the loader caches.
examples.good: The loader caches every resolved path.

rules.fix: Delete the signpost, or link the named section.

citation.note: Mechanizable as a token list, so no judgement partner. Complements prose-craft.directional-ref, which owns the POSITION-dependent forms ("see below", "the table above") as substitutions with named replacements; these are the READING-ORDER forms, whose fix is deletion, not substitution. Upstream ai-tells.RestatementMarkers and ai-tells.SelfReference overlap.

rules.name: Delete emoji used as list markers
rules.message: emoji list marker: {match} -- delete it; the list marker carries the structure
rules.fix: Delete the emoji; use a plain list marker.

citation.source: AI tells catalog — formatting.md ("Emoji as list markers or in headings")
citation.note: The list-marker half of the catalog row. The heading half is already mechanised as prose-format.emoji-heading, which the source repo gates at warning; this rule reaches the list position that `scope: heading` cannot see. Same codepoint ranges, `scope: raw` because a list marker is markdown syntax. The 2026-09-12 audit made the markdown list marker mandatory: the optional form also matched an emoji opening a plain paragraph ("WARN **Whoa there!**" in an error message), which is emoji residue but not a list marker, and one such line in pre-2022 human prose. GO->PYTHON: the pattern holds the literal characters. Python `regex` rejects `\x{...}`, and PCRE2 rejects `\u` and `\U`; literals work in both.
